text: AI guardrails do not work. I'm going to say that one more time. Guardrails do not work. If someone is determined enough to trick GPT-5, they're going to deal with that guardrail. No problem.
speaker: Sander Schulhoff
context: At the opening of this podcast, Sander makes his most provocative statement about AI security. AI guardrails are large language models trained to classify whether inputs and outputs to AI systems are valid or malicious, essentially acting as security filters. Sander, who runs AI red teaming competitions and works with leading AI labs on model defenses, has found through extensive testing that these guardrails are easily bypassed by determined attackers and provide a false sense of security.
text_ko: AI 가드레일(guardrails)은 효과가 없어요. 다시 한 번 말할게요. 가드레일은 효과가 없어요. 누군가 GPT-5를 속일 만큼 결심했다면 그 가드레일을 우회하거나 무력화할 거예요. 문제없어요.
text_zh: AI 那些所谓的安全护栏（guardrails）根本不管用。我再说一遍：安全护栏（guardrails）根本不管用。如果有人铁了心要骗过 GPT-5（GPT-5），他们总能把这些护栏绕过去，完全没问题。
text_es: Las medidas de contención para la IA (AI guardrails) no funcionan. Lo voy a repetir: no funcionan. Si alguien está tan decidido a burlar a GPT‑5, va a saltarse esa medida sin problema.
original_text: AI guardrails do not work. I'm going to say that one more time. Guardrails do not work. If someone is determined enough to trick GPT-5, they're going to deal with that guardrail. No problem. When these guardrail providers say, "We catch everything," that's a complete lie.

text: You can patch a bug, but you can't patch a brain. If you find some bug in your software and you go and patch it, you can be maybe 99.99% sure that bug is solved. Try to do that in your AI system.
speaker: Sander Schulhoff
context: Sander explains why AI security is fundamentally different from traditional cybersecurity. In traditional software, when you identify and fix a bug, you can be confident it's permanently resolved. However, AI systems based on neural networks don't work like traditional code - they're more like 'brains' that can be tricked in countless unpredictable ways, making it nearly impossible to definitively solve security vulnerabilities.
text_ko: 버그는 패치할 수 있지만, 뇌는 패치할 수 없어요. 소프트웨어(software)에서 버그(bug)를 찾아 패치(patch)하면 그 버그가 거의 99.99% 해결됐다고 확신할 수 있어요. 그걸 AI 시스템(AI system)에서 해보세요.
text_es: Puedes parchear un fallo (bug), pero no un cerebro. Si encuentras un fallo en tu software y lo parcheas, puedes estar prácticamente 99,99% seguro de que está solucionado. Intenta hacer eso en tu sistema de IA (AI).
key_sentence: You can patch a bug, but you can't patch a brain with 99.99% surety.
original_text: You can patch a bug, but you can't patch a brain. If you find some bug in your software and you go and patch it, you can be maybe 99.99% sure that bug is solved. Try to do that in your AI system. You can be 99.99% sure that the problem is still there.

text: I found through running these events is that they are terribly, terribly insecure and frankly, they don't work. They just don't work.
speaker: Sander Schulhoff
context: Lenny asks Sander about the problem he discovered with AI security defenses. Sander has been running AI red teaming competitions for years, studying various defense mechanisms including AI guardrails. Through these competitions, where teams attempt to break AI systems, he has consistently found that guardrails - which are supposed to detect and block malicious inputs and outputs - are easily defeated by attackers.
text_ko: 제가 이런 이벤트들을 직접 운영해 보면서 알게 된 건, 정말 심각하게 불안정하고 솔직히 말해서 제대로 작동하지 않는다는 거예요. 그냥 안 돼요.
text_zh: 我办这些活动下来发现，效果真的是很不稳定，说白了就是不管用。就是不行。
text_es: Lo que descubrí organizando estos eventos es que son terriblemente, pero terriblemente inseguros y, siendo honestos, simplemente no funcionan. No funcionan y ya.
key_sentence: These events are terribly, terribly insecure and frankly, they don't work.

vocabulary.definition: Lacking confidence or assurance; uncertain and anxious about oneself or one's abilities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being insecure can refer to a lack of confidence in one's decisions, strategies, or the stability of a company, which can hinder effective leadership and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'insecure' often has a negative connotation, it can also indicate a level of self-awareness that prompts individuals to seek improvement.

text: The number of possible attacks against another LLM is equivalent to the number of possible prompts. Each possible prompt could be an attack. And for a model like GPT-5, the number of possible attacks is one followed by a million zeros.
speaker: Sander Schulhoff
context: Sander explains why measuring the effectiveness of AI guardrails is fundamentally flawed. When guardrail companies claim they catch "99% of attacks," they're working with a virtually infinite attack space. Since every possible text prompt could potentially be crafted as an attack, the search space for potential exploits is astronomically large - far beyond what any security system can realistically test against or defend.
text_ko: 다른 대형 언어 모델(LLM)을 겨냥한 가능한 공격의 수는 가능한 프롬프트(prompt)의 수와 똑같아요. 가능한 각 프롬프트가 공격이 될 수 있고, GPT-5 같은 모델에서는 그 수가 1 뒤에 0이 백만 개나 붙는 엄청난 수예요.
text_zh: 对另一个LLM的潜在攻击数量，基本上就等于可能的提示词(prompt)数量。每个提示词都有可能成为攻击手段。像GPT-5这种模型，可能的攻击方式简直是天文数字，后面得跟上百万个零。
text_es: El número de posibles ataques contra otro modelo de lenguaje (LLM) es equivalente al número de prompts posibles. Cualquier prompt podría ser un ataque. Y para un modelo como GPT-5, estamos hablando de un número de ataques posibles que es un uno seguido de un millón de ceros.
key_sentence: The number of possible attacks is equivalent to one followed by a million zeros.

text: The smartest artificial intelligence researchers in the world are working at Frontier Labs like OpenAI, Google, Anthropic. They can't solve this problem. They haven't been able to solve this problem in the last couple years of large language models being popular.
speaker: Sander Schulhoff
context: Sander is explaining why enterprise AI security companies' claims to solve prompt injection and jailbreaking don't make sense. He argues that if the most advanced AI research teams at leading companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic - who have the best researchers and unlimited resources - cannot solve adversarial robustness, it's unrealistic to expect smaller enterprise security companies to have cracked this fundamental problem.
text_ko: 세계에서 가장 똑똑한 인공지능 연구자들이 OpenAI, Google, Anthropic 같은 최첨단 연구소에서 일하고 있어요. 그런데 그들도 이 문제를 못 풀고 있어요. 대규모 언어 모델(large language models)이 인기 있었던 지난 몇 년 동안에도 해결하지 못했어요.
text_zh: 全世界最顶尖的AI研究人员都在那些前沿实验室工作，比如OpenAI、谷歌、Anthropic这些公司。连他们都搞不定这个问题。大语言模型(large language models)火了这么几年，他们到现在还是没能解决这个问题。
text_es: Los investigadores de inteligencia artificial más brillantes del mundo están trabajando en laboratorios de vanguardia como OpenAI, Google, Anthropic. Y no han podido resolver este problema. En estos últimos años, con todo el boom de los modelos de lenguaje grandes (large language models), siguen sin encontrarle la vuelta.
key_sentence: Frontier Labs researchers can't solve this problem with large language models.

vocabulary.definition: Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines, particularly computer systems, enabling them to perform tasks such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, AI is leveraged to enhance decision-making, automate processes, and improve customer experiences, driving efficiency and innovation across various sectors.
vocabulary.nuance: While AI can imply advanced machine learning capabilities, it is important to specify the type of AI being discussed, as the term can encompass a wide range of technologies from basic automation to sophisticated neural networks.

vocabulary.definition: Large language models (LLMs) are advanced AI systems designed to understand and generate human language, trained on vast datasets to perform tasks such as translation, summarization, and content generation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, LLMs are utilized for applications ranging from chatbots and virtual assistants to content creation and data analysis, significantly enhancing productivity and user engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: While LLMs are powerful tools for natural language processing, they may also raise concerns regarding bias, accuracy, and ethical considerations in their deployment.

text: There's not an incredible amount of value in just doing AI red teaming. And I suppose there'll be... I don't know if I want to say that. It's possible that there will be less value in just doing classical cybersecurity work.
speaker: Sander Schulhoff
context: Sander discusses career opportunities in AI security, specifically addressing where he sees the most valuable work happening. While pure AI red teaming (attacking AI systems) and traditional cybersecurity remain important, he believes the intersection of these fields - understanding both classical security principles and AI-specific vulnerabilities - represents the most critical and valuable skill set for future security professionals.
text_ko: 그냥 AI 레드팀(AI red teaming)만 하는 것으로는 엄청난 가치가 나오진 않아요. 그리고 이 말을 해도 되나 싶긴 한데요, 어쩌면 전통적인 사이버보안 업무(classical cybersecurity work)만으로 얻는 가치도 줄어들 수 있어요.
text_zh: 光做AI红队测试(AI red teaming)本身，价值其实不大。我也不知道该不该这么说，但光做传统网络安全工作(classical cybersecurity work)的价值可能也会更低。
text_es: No aporta mucho valor limitarse únicamente al red teaming de IA (AI red teaming). Y supongo que... no sé si quiero decirlo, pero puede que también haya menos valor en ceñirse al trabajo clásico de ciberseguridad (classical cybersecurity work).
key_sentence: There's not an incredible amount of value in just doing AI red teaming.
original_text: There's not an incredible amount of value in just doing AI red teaming. And I suppose there'll be... I don't know if I want to say that. It's possible that there will be less value in just doing classical cybersecurity work. But where those two meet is, it's just going to be a job of great, great importance.

vocabulary.definition: The importance, worth, or usefulness of something, often measured in terms of financial gain or strategic advantage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'value' often refers to the benefits derived from a product, service, or investment, and is crucial for decision-making and strategy development.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'value' can refer to monetary worth, it can also encompass intangible benefits such as brand reputation or customer loyalty, making context important for its use.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of protecting systems, networks, and programs from digital attacks, theft, or damage.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, cybersecurity is essential for safeguarding sensitive information and maintaining trust with customers and stakeholders, especially in an era of increasing cyber threats.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with IT departments, cybersecurity also has broader implications for organizational risk management and compliance, highlighting its importance across all business functions.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to traditional methods or established principles, often contrasted with modern or innovative approaches.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of cybersecurity, 'classical' methods may refer to conventional practices that have been used historically, which may be less effective against contemporary threats.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'classical' can imply reliability and proven effectiveness, it may also suggest a lack of innovation or adaptability in rapidly changing environments.
